clue.text: Get new staff — or get new owners

definitions.meaning: hands are workers, so to change them is to take on fresh staff
property that passes from one owner to another is said to do this

explanation.surface: A business either hires a fresh workforce or is sold to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands means workers, giving the literal sense; the idiom means property passing to a new owner.

clue.text: It's heavenly to play, but there are strings attached

definitions.text: It's heavenly to play, but there are strings attached

parts.words: It's heavenly to play, but there are strings attached
parts.note: angels are pictured playing this stringed instrument in heaven; strings attached is a pun on the idiom for conditions

explanation.surface: Something delightful comes with conditions, as the idiom about strings attached says.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels in paintings play this instrument, and it is literally fitted with strings.

clue.text: Out of gear?

parts.note: gear here means clothing, so out of it means unclothed, not a car out of gear

explanation.surface: A question about a car slipped into neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has taken off all their gear, or clothes, is naked.

clue.text: Honour a merger of Ben and Noel

indicators.note: a merger blends the two names together, so their letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Two men named Ben and Noel joining forces are given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a merger of' mixes the letters of BEN and NOEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the nobility, or to dignify them, is to honour them; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A parliamentarian's creating measures in power

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
the apostrophe-s supplies the letter S

explanation.surface: An MP is wielding power by bringing in new measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of electric current, such as those listed on a power supply, are measured in these.

clue.text: Fool perhaps having braided hair put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is written bottom to top, so it is read backwards

parts.note: tressed means having hair arranged in tresses or braids

explanation.surface: A jester with a braided hairstyle has it pinned up.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a creamy fruit pudding, such as gooseberry fool; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a pudding of fruit purée and cream, an example of a sweet course.

clue.text: Understood to be arrested

definitions.meaning: to apprehend an idea is to grasp or comprehend it
police apprehend a suspect when they seize them

explanation.surface: A suspect realises the charge as they are taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: grasping mentally and seizing physically, both in the past tense here.

clue.text: Wild world opens around a cat used to wintry weather

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild landscape opens up around a cat adapted to snowy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' mixes the letters of WORLD OPENS with A; 'around' merely links the A to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This big cat lives in the high mountains of Central Asia and is well adapted to cold and snow.

clue.text: Frank is ready to do business

definitions.meaning: a shop is like this when trading for the day

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is keen to start trading.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both candid in speech and, of a shop, trading and accepting customers.

clue.text: Commercial mail for a remote business centre

parts.note: trading is commercial activity, buying and selling
post is mail, letters and parcels

explanation.surface: Junk mail advertising arrives for a distant office.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier station where goods were exchanged, often in a remote area, was a centre of business.

clue.text: Drag minor back

indicators.note: back says the word for the minor is read from right to left

parts.note: a ward is a minor under the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a child back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull or haul something along is to drag it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Keeps on the beach, they may be soon liquidated

definitions.text: Keeps on the beach, they may be soon liquidated

parts.words: Keeps on the beach, they may be soon liquidated
parts.note: keeps are castle towers built here of sand, and liquidated puns on the tide washing them away

explanation.surface: Businesses holding stock at the seaside may soon go bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Children build castles of sand on the shore, with keeps and towers, and the incoming tide melts them away.

clue.text: Vehicles drawn up in accordance with the law

definitions.meaning: a conveyance is a means of transport such as a cart or carriage

definitions.text: drawn up in accordance with the law
definitions.meaning: a conveyance is also a legal deed transferring property, drawn up by a lawyer

explanation.surface: Carriages are pulled up beside a court as the law requires.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both a means of transport and a legal document transferring title to property.

clue.text: Messenger has job getting in beer

indicators.note: the job word gets into the beer word, sitting inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A courier has a job that involves fetching the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The disciples sent out to spread the gospel were messengers; the Greek root means one sent forth.

clue.text: One-time rising group crack up?

parts.note: ex means former, one-time

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for the group is written upwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A former band climbing the charts is breaking down with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: To crack someone up is to praise them highly; the question mark flags this sense rather than laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up somebody is an idiom for praising them highly, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: In an old-fashioned way, please

parts.note: the archaic word for please, a shortening of I pray thee

explanation.surface: A polite request made in a quaint style.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic contraction of I pray thee was used to ask politely, the old way of saying please.

clue.text: Song from little Sarah, piercing in the afternoon

indicators.note: piercing says the name goes into the middle of the afternoon letters

parts.note: p.m. marks the afternoon
Sal is a short form of Sarah

explanation.surface: A girl's shrill song cuts through the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song or hymn, especially one of those in the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: To be readily available, part of index is typeset

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A book's index is set in type so that it can be consulted easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is present and found in the world simply is, or is there to be had.

clue.text: Singer very keen to retire

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: avid means very keen or eager

explanation.surface: A vocalist is eager to stop performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, especially of opera.

clue.text: Bargain crop

definitions.meaning: to crop is to cut, as with scissors

explanation.surface: A cheap deal on harvested produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a cheap purchase in British slang and also a quick cut with scissors.

clue.text: Toys sold out around end of April

indicators.note: around says the mixed letters go around the single letter
out means put out of order, so the letters of sold are mixed
end of picks the last letter of April

explanation.surface: Toys sold out by the end of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SOLD into DOLS, and 'around' puts that round L, the last letter of April, picked by 'end of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolls are figures that children play with, examples of toys.

clue.text: Light diet may upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A light diet may upset the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective describing the diet, but it is the definition: daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of daylight are the light part of the day, so light can stand for that period.

clue.text: Class of fighters, in the East

definitions.text: Class of fighters, in the East

parts.words: Class of fighters, in the East
parts.note: the warrior caste of feudal Japan

explanation.surface: A description of an Eastern military caste.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the hereditary warrior caste of feudal Japan, a class of Eastern fighters.

clue.text: Awful deep

definitions.meaning: the word also means immeasurably deep, like an abyss

explanation.surface: Something terrible and profound.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means dreadful in everyday use and, literally, bottomless like an abyss.

clue.text: Somebody's rubber

parts.note: rubber is read as one who rubs, a person who gives massages, not an eraser

explanation.surface: Someone's pencil eraser is being claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages rubs people's muscles, so he is literally a rubber.

clue.text: She'll be a fool if she comes back

indicators.note: comes back says the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.surface: A woman will be foolish if she returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for any girl's name; reversing A NIT gives one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tina is a female first name, so it can stand for a she.

clue.text: Obscure blemish

explanation.surface: Hiding a spot on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make unclear and the noun means a smudge or stain.

clue.text: Whisky drinkers may say that it's just a question of time

definitions.meaning: someone having water added to their whisky says this word to signal stop

definitions.text: it's just a question of time
definitions.meaning: the word asks at what time

explanation.surface: Drinkers say that getting drunk is just a matter of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinker being poured a measure calls out this word to stop the pour; it is also the question word asking what time.

clue.text: A sign of more to follow

definitions.text: A sign of more to follow

parts.words: A sign of more to follow
parts.note: the mathematical sign for addition, meaning more is being added

explanation.surface: An omen that more is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The addition sign indicates that something more is to be added.

clue.text: Enormously powerful ocean destroyer

parts.note: not a warship but the orca, a huge predator of the sea

explanation.surface: A description of a mighty naval warship.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is a huge, powerful predator of the oceans that kills seals and even other whales.

clue.text: Lacking opener, drain pitcher

indicators.note: lacking its opener means the first letter of the drain word is dropped

parts.note: a sewer is a drain for waste

explanation.surface: A jug pours poorly because its drain has no opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitcher' looks like a baseball player but is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug, and this is a wide-mouthed water jug.

clue.text: Confirm new bits are news

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh snippets are being reported as news and need checking.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify to something as true is to confirm it; the idiom means give evidence.
